summary: ExoSpace is a smart telemetry and ergonomics platform designed to improve astronaut safety, comfort and performance during Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) and space missions. The project aims to develop a tracking system that collects and analyses data related to astronauts' physical conditions and exoskeleton performance. By monitoring factors such as movement, physical strain and equipment related data, ExoSpace aims to identify potential ergonomic problems and provide meaningful feedback. This allows  mission units to better understand the physical demands placed on astronauts, recognize possible risks and make more informed decisions about equipment adjustments and mission conditions. The importance of ExoSpace lies in the challenges astronauts face in space, where limited mobility, demanding physical tasks and unfamiliar environmental conditions can increase physical strain. By combining telemetry analysis with ergonomic insights, the platform intends to support safer operations  while contributing to the development of future astronaut support technologies.
details: Exospace is an intelligent exoskeleton and health tracking system developed to prevent critical health problems such as muscle wasting and physical fatigue experienced by astronauts staying in space for long periods transforming this exoskeleton which does more than just provide physicals support into a smart data platform the software displays instant muscle maps over a 3D body model and automatically adjusts the resistance of the exoskeleton by predicting fatigue risks thanks to artificial intelligence capable of working uninterrupted against possible internet and communication disconnects in spacecraft this smart system takes it power from Nasa open data sources offering both an east to use interface for astronauts and a detailed tracking panel for doctors on Earth
